Position Overview: 

As Android Developer, you will build and evolve the native Android app that Showpad's field sellers rely on every day to find content, learn, and engage with buyers, often on the road and with patchy connectivity. You'll work in a mature, modular codebase, helping to move it towards a cleaner, more testable architecture while continuing to ship new features.

You'll operate with a high degree of ownership, collaborate closely with product, design and backend peers, and help raise the technical bar of the mobile team.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Android Engineering: Design, build and maintain features in Kotlin (with some legacy Java) across a multi-module Gradle project, placing new code in dedicated feature modules rather than the historical core module.

- Architecture Evolution: Drive the gradual migration from MVP-style Presenter/UseCase screens to Hilt-injected ViewModels built on Coroutines and Flow (StateFlow/SharedFlow), keeping each migration a small, reviewable change.

- Networking & Data: Build resilient API integrations with Retrofit, using consistent result handling and cancellation-safe coroutines, and moving away from deprecated networking libraries.

- Offline & Sync: Build and maintain offline content availability, background sync (WorkManager) and local storage (Room, encrypted files).

- UI Development: Build and maintain screens using XML layouts and ViewBinding, delivering accessible, responsive experiences across phones and tablets. Knowledge of Jetpack Compose may be beneficial as we develop the application.

- Integrations & Content: Work on features that connect to Salesforce, SAML login, web content in WebViews with JavaScript bridges (ShowpadJS)and Chrome Custom Tabs, and in-app document and PDF viewing.

- Quality & Testing: Write and maintain unit tests (JUnit 4, Mockito, Robole ctric) and instrumentation tests, and contribute to the automated test pipeline.

- Build, Release & Observability: Contribute to GitLab CI pipelines and release builds (build types, R8 minification, signing, a dedicated China build), and use crash reporting and product analytics (Crashlytics, Pendo, Segment) to find and fix real-world issues.

- Security & Compliance: Apply secure-by-default practices to credential handling, data storage and network traffic, in line with GDPR and SOC 2 expectations.

- Collaboration & Growth: Participate actively in design and code reviews, contribute to team documentation, module maps and conventions, and mentor fellow engineers.

Are you our next Android Engineer?

Must haves

- Software engineering experience, including significant time building production Android apps in a SaaS or enterprise environment

- Strong proficiency in Kotlin, with a working knowledge of Java for maintaining legacy code

- Hands-on experience with Coroutines and Flow, Hilt/Dagger, and Retrofit

- Experience with MVVM and other architectural patterns, and with gradually migrating legacy code to them

- Experience working in multi-module Gradle projects

- Experience building offline-first apps, including local storage, background sync and patchy connectivity

- Comfortable working in a mixed legacy and modern codebase

- A solid testing mindset: unit testing with JUnit, Mockito and Robolectric

- Good communication skills and a collaborative, team-first approach to engineering

- Reads and writes clear technical documentation, such as module maps and conventions

Nice to haves

- Experience with XML/ViewBinding UIs, and with Jetpack Compose, which would help as the UI evolves

- Familiarity with CI/CD for mobile (GitLab CI, Fastlane or similar), R8/ProGuard and Play Store release management

- Experience with product analytics and crash reporting (Pendo, Segment, Firebase Crashlytics)

- Prior exposure to CRM platforms (Salesforce or similar), SAML/SSO flows, or PDF and document rendering

- Awareness of mobile security and compliance fundamentals (GDPR, SOC 2)

- Experience shipping apps for multiple regions, including builds with region-specific constraints

- Experience building and versioning shared internal libraries

- Experience with Android WebView: JS bridges, security hardening (URL allowlists, disabling unneeded file access) and debugging web content inside an app
